newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche-MGAM saga may have hit 180,000 clients.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche-MGAM saga may have hit 180,000 clients.

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Bank AG on Monday described as "realistic" a press report that some 180,000 clients might be affected by last year's alleged funds mismanagement incident at its London arm MGAM.
However the bank said the client figure, reported in the mass-circulation daily Bild, would not mean it needed to make additional compensation payments.

A spokesman said Deutsche had estimated its compensation needs on the basis of the volume of funds on deposit at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), not on the number of individuals with accounts.
"We said last December that around 90,000 MGAM accounts were involved in this but we were never quite sure how many people were behind that number," the spokesman said.
"The number of clients (mentioned in the press) appears to us to be realistic. But this has no effect on the compensation figure."
Deutsche has said it will face a 200 million pound ($327 million) compensation charge for alleged mismanagement at three MGAM unit trusts last year -- an incident that came to light in September.
That charge comes on top of a 180-million pound net injection by the bank to shore up the ailing unit trusts.
The bank set aside between 1.1 and 1.2 billion marks ($646-$705 million) in its 1996 results to cover damages related to MGAM.
British investment watchdog IMRO last week imposed a record two million pound fine on MGAM over the debacle, which led to the dismissal of Peter Young, who managed two of the funds.
--Catherine O'Mahony, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 0.612 British Pounds) ($ = 1.702 German Marks)
